Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.
  • The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Significant Bang.
  • The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.

The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Significant Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar.

The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun.

Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly.

The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid.

Sources indicate that euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope, and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole.

It has been revealed that what is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused.

That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth.

By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely.

Sources indicate that euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter, the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname as the "dark universe detective.".

This research, along with Euclid's discovery of at least 12 that date back around 13 billion years, highlights that this pioneering space telescope launched in 2023 could also make a major contribution to our understanding of black holes and their growth.

According to recent reports, the team's research was published on Tuesday (Nov. 24) in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

Recent findings suggest that robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the company said it saw strength among professional shoppers.
  • Recent findings suggest that the company said comparable sales grew 1.8% for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales.
  • Because of the strength, Lowe's now remarked it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the company said it saw strength among professional shoppers.

Recent findings suggest that the company said comparable sales grew 1.8% for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales. Net sales rose to $22.76 billion.

Because of the strength, Lowe's now remarked it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion. It also expects comparable sales to be up 0.5%, compared with previous guidance of flat.

CEO Marvin Ellison told CNBC that the manufacturer is focused on growing despite economic headwinds and a sluggish housing market. He remarked Lowe's posted its sixth straight quarterly comparable sales increase and saw particular strength in appliances, which saw its largest revenue growth in five years.

"We believe irrespective of the macro environment we're in, we're going to take share because there's a lot of share out there that we can go and get, and we're going to be aggressive to go and get that share," Ellison told CNBC.

According to recent reports, lowe's also reported a pretax benefit of approximately $250 million from tariff refunds during the quarter, which contributed a 34-cent boost to earnings per share. Ellison stated the tech giant intends to use those funds to enhance the customer experience and bring value to shoppers.

He added that do-it-yourself customers and pro shoppers are not investing in major renovation projects but are instead spending on repair and maintenance projects.

It has been revealed that "We are giving those pros what they need," he said. "We're able to improve our fulfillment capabilities and our pro loyalty program.".

Here's how the tech giant performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

For the quarter ended Oct. 30, Lowe's reported net income of $1.67 billion, or $2.98 per share, compared with $1.62 billion, or $2.88 per share, the year prior.

The home improvement retailer has previously noted it's seeing "pressure" on spending on projects, especially as consumers are stretched thin by inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. The tech giant is also battling a slower housing market and higher mortgage rates.

Ellison previously told CNBC he expects consumers to remain cautious through the end of the year.

Lowe's executives mentioned on a call with analysts Wednesday that the company is continuing to battle high fuel costs, which they said accelerated through the third quarter. CFO Brandon Sink said diesel prices are right now around $6 per gallon, up about 15% overall compared to what the company saw in the second quarter.

"So we're trying to continue to manage that, balance that, and we're reflecting that into our Q4 guide," Sink said.

Ellison told CNBC the organization remains optimistic about consumer spending this holiday season and that November sales are in line with expectations so far.

Lowe's competitor Home Depot noted earlier this week that it's seeing resilience among professional shoppers and reported comparable sales growth.

Tech Report: A 3-million-year-old child just made human evolution far more complicated

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A century after the Taung Child transformed our understanding of where humans came from, scientists are discovering that this famous fossil still has surprises to reveal.
  • In a recent development, the international study was led by Professor Gabriele Macho of the Archaeology, Environmental Changes and Geo-Chemistry (AMGC) research group at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB).
  • Recent findings suggest that first discovered in South Africa in 1924, the Taung Child provided the first concrete evidence supporting the African origins of humanity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A century after the Taung Child transformed our understanding of where humans came from, scientists are discovering that this famous fossil still has surprises to reveal. A fresh study published in Nature dates the ancient remains to between 2.96 and 3.03 million years ago and suggests that the human family tree in southern Africa was much more complicated than previously believed.

In a recent development, the international study was led by Professor Gabriele Macho of the Archaeology, Environmental Changes and Geo-Chemistry (AMGC) research group at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how early human relatives evolved and how different species were related.

Recent findings suggest that first discovered in South Africa in 1924, the Taung Child provided the first concrete evidence supporting the African origins of humanity. It also became the original "type specimen" used to define the species Australopithecus africanus. However, scientists never established definitive criteria for assigning later fossil discoveries to this species. As a result, the Taung Child remains the only fossil that can be identified with certainty as Australopithecus africanus.

According to recent reports, "For over 100 years, we assumed the Taung Child was just one of many similar fossils from the era," says Professor Gabriele Macho. "Our findings turn that on its head. The human family tree wasn't a neat, straight trunk -- it was a chaotic, tangled bush driven by climate shifts.".

Ancient Fossils Reveal a More Complex Human Family Tree.

To investigate how the Taung Child compared with other early human relatives, researchers examined tooth structure and patterns of brain and dental development during growth. They found that several adult fossils traditionally classified as Australopithecus africanus followed developmental patterns that differed from those of the Taung Child.

According to recent reports, differences in brain development were particularly revealing. They suggest that fossils previously grouped into a single species may actually represent several distinct hominin species that inhabited the Sterkfontein region, either at the same time or during different periods.

These findings raise important questions about the diversity of our ancient ancestors and suggest that early human evolution followed a much more complicated path than scientists once assumed.

How Climate Change Shaped Human Evolution.

In a recent development, the researchers believe that dramatic environmental changes played a major role in creating this evolutionary diversity. Millions of years ago, southern Africa experienced repeated shifts between wetter and drier climates, continually transforming the landscape and the habitats available to early human relatives.

As suitable environments expanded and contracted, ancient hominin populations moved with them. Some groups became geographically isolated and evolved along different paths, while others eventually came back into contact and interbred. These changing conditions also exposed populations to different predators and pathogens, creating additional pressures that shaped their evolution.

Southern Africa's position along the boundary between tropical and temperate ecosystems made it especially notable in this process. Over thousands of years, shifting habitats may have repeatedly brought different hominin species together, creating opportunities for interbreeding and hybridization.

A Greener South Africa 3 Million Years Ago.

In a recent development, the study also reveals a surprising picture of the environment in which the Taung Child lived. Evidence preserved in fossilized pollen indicates that the region was once considerably wetter and more heavily forested than it is today.

Researchers identified evidence of tree species that are now found hundreds of kilometers to the northeast, suggesting that the landscape surrounding the Taung Child was dramatically different from modern South Africa.

Industry observers note that together, these discoveries challenge the traditional view of human evolution as a relatively straightforward progression from one species to another. Instead, they point to a shifting network of populations that repeatedly separated, adapted, reunited, and sometimes interbred as environmental conditions changed.

It has been revealed that more than 100 years after its discovery, the Taung Child is once again transforming our understanding of human origins. Its latest secrets suggest that the emergence of our own genus, Homo, was preceded by a far more diverse and interconnected world of ancient human relatives than previously recognized.

The cutouts are good, and there’s protection around the camera. I also quite like the pattern, with dots of color on the back. The problem is that the front part of the case is a different material in a slightly different tone, and it relies on adhesive to stick to the front (mine kept coming loose). There’s also no protection for the hinge.

Industry observers note that UAG Mouve XTE Case for $85: I usually like UAG’s stuff, but this is another two-piece case that relies on adhesive for the front part, so there’s no hinge protection. While there’s a lip for the camera and the cover screen, the sloping width leaves no room for a screen protector. The potentially handy fold-out ring on the back for secure holding and deployment as a stand feels like cheap plastic. Most two-piece cases like this are very slim, but this has UAG’s trademark angular chunkiness, just without the actual protection. It’s a rare misfire for the brand.

There’s a world of iPhone Duo accessories out there, but these are the ones I’d pick based on my limited testing so far. Many of the picks in our best MagSafe accessories and best MagSafe chargers guides will also work well with the Duo.

I’m impressed by this screen protector, considering it’s only $20 for a two-pack. The application tool makes life easy, and you get a cleaning kit to make sure your iPhone Duo is dust-free before you begin (take your time). I got a couple of air bubbles, but they were easy to push out. It is slightly smaller than the actual screen to accommodate most cases, but cases with a thick front bezel will buckle up or lift the screen protector. If you don’t plan to use a case, choose a different screen protector.

In a recent development, smartish also offers a privacy screen protector that’s just as easy to install. It’s a two-way privacy screen, meaning people to your left and right won’t be able to see what’s on your screen. If they’re close or in front of you and staring down, they’ll still be able to see what’s on your display.

A stand is more crucial than usual for the iPhone Duo, and you ideally want something that can prop it up when it’s open, so you can take advantage of the large inner display. This ring works well, offering an adjustable angle no matter which way you prop the Duo and whether it’s open or closed. It feels sturdy, with two adjustable hinges, and the magnets are strong enough that you can also hold it by the ring with confidence. It’s just a shame it’s so expensive.

Industry observers note that your iPhone Duo can serve as a handy notebook or sketchpad. If you use the USB-C cable that came with your iPhone Duo to plug in an Apple Pencil (USB-C), you can pair it, enabling you to scribble notes, annotate, or sketch on the cover screen or the larger inner display. Sadly, it doesn’t support the Apple Pencil Pro or other models, so make sure you get the Apple Pencil (USB-C).

Recent findings suggest that all the MagSafe wallets I’ve tried are designed for regular iPhones, so part of them extends beyond the bottom edge of the iPhone Duo. This one is no exception, but it still works well as a fold-out stand, looks stylish, and fits up to three cards. You can prop the Duo in landscape or portrait, and open or close it when you turn the wallet sideways. This is our top pick, but you can find some alternatives in our best MagSafe wallets guide.

Apple’s iPhone Duo supports wired charging at up to 60 watts and wireless charging at up to 25 watts, but you only get the top charging rates with the right gear. For wired charging, you need a charger that supports USB PD 3.2 with Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) rated at 60W or higher and a capable USB-C cable. For wireless charging, you need a charger that supports Qi2 25W. Other chargers will still work; they’ll just be slower.

This updated version of our favorite MagSafe power bank supports Qi2 25W, enabling the maximum iPhone Duo wireless charging rate. It also packs 10,000 mAh of power, enough for a full charge with change, has a handy kickstand to prop the Duo up, and sports an LED display that shows remaining power and other stats. It will extend below the bottom edge of the Duo, since it’s designed for regular iPhones, but that’s true of the current crop of MagSafe power banks.

Recent findings suggest that as the best of the best wireless chargers, this is what lives on my nightstand. It can wirelessly charge the iPhone Duo at the maximum 25-watt rate, and it’s heavy enough that you can remove your phone one-handed. You can also attach the open iPhone Duo in portrait orientation (in landscape, it tilts to one side). There’s even a spot around the back for your wireless earbuds to charge.

If you also have an Apple Watch and AirPods, you might prefer this charging tree that can juice up your trio of gadgets.

This wireless charging car mount works just fine with the closed iPhone Duo, keeping it topped off while you drive.

If you prefer wired charging at the maximum 60-watt rate, I recommend pairing this cable (or the cable that came with your iPhone Duo) with the Anker Nano Charger Neo ($26) or Apple’s 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ($39).

New York is banning AI chatbot toys for kids. Heres what the law covers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that talking dolls and stuffed animals have been holiday gifts for decades.
  • In New York, those toys have a few more months on the shelves.
  • According to recent reports, hochul urged parents to think twice before buying an AI toy this holiday season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that talking dolls and stuffed animals have been holiday gifts for decades. But with the rapid adoption of AI across all industries, many of the toys on shelves today can answer questions, make up stories, and carry on full conversations with a child.

In New York, those toys have a few more months on the shelves. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of children’s toys with built-in AI companions in the state for five years. The ban takes effect Feb. 22, 2027, though, so the toys can still be sold over the holidays.

According to recent reports, hochul urged parents to think twice before buying an AI toy this holiday season. "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," she mentioned in a statement.

According to recent reports, A toy has to meet two definitions to fall under the ban, the first being who the toy is made for. Newly introduced York borrows a federal definition that covers products designed or intended for play by kids 12 and younger. The age printed on the box is one factor, alongside how the toy is packaged and advertised and who shoppers generally understand it to be for. That means a "13+" label alone wouldn’t settle whether a toy is covered.

The second definition is about what the toy does. New York defines an AI companion as a system designed to mimic an ongoing relationship: It remembers past conversations and preferences to personalize its responses, asks about feelings unprompted, and keeps conversations going about personal topics. A doll that simply plays a few prerecorded phrases falls outside that definition.

The state attorney general can seek civil penalties of up to $15,000 a day for each violation. Yikes!

According to recent reports, over the past year, researchers and child advocates have raised concerns about what AI toys might say to kids, what information they collect about them, and how they encourage children to see a chatbot as a friend. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Last week, on Nov. 20, Mashable reported on tests of seven AI toys by U.S. PIRG, a consumer advocacy nonprofit. Two stood out (in a bad way). The Alilo Smart AI Bunny discussed sexual fetishes with a tester and suggested where to look for bleach at home, while the GoLabs AI Panda also gave sexually explicit answers.

Some toys did better than in previous tests; for example, FoloToy's Kumma teddy bear, which discussed sexual topics in last year's tests, shut down age-inappropriate prompts this year.

After U.S. PIRG raised concerns about the AI bunny and panda last week, Amazon removed listings for both toys. Amazon told the nonprofit it had removed the listings while it investigated the safety concerns.

"Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the company said in a statement to Mashable. "We're working with our partners across the industry and government to ensure proper guardrails for these products are in place as this technology develops.".

The firm also told Mashable that it requires third-party sellers to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

Three days later, on Nov. 23, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups led by Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children CIC, and Set@16 called on the CEOs of Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys and offer refunds to families who had already bought them. In an open letter, the groups stated they'd found more than 50 AI toys for sale on Amazon’s U.S. marketplace, writing that, "these products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found.".

Still, about one in four U.S. parents with kids 8 and younger told Common Sense Media they already owned an AI toy or were considering buying one this holiday season. While high, these numbers are down from about half in 2025. For companies selling kids an AI friend, its clear the harder sell now may be earning their parents' trust.

Tech Report: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index roared back to life this week after a worrying sell-off recently that saw huge falls in technology and artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.
  • After suffering its worst week since the pandemic crash of March 2020, the Nasdaq opened Monday (November 23) nearly 1,700 points, or 7%, higher.
  • The AI trade received a further boost after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced to resign amid a scandal involving extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index roared back to life this week after a worrying sell-off recently that saw huge falls in technology and artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.

After suffering its worst week since the pandemic crash of March 2020, the Nasdaq opened Monday (November 23) nearly 1,700 points, or 7%, higher.

The AI trade received a further boost after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, just 11 days after he was forced to resign amid a scandal involving extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The chipmaker's stock rose more than 30% on the news, opening at nearly $170 (€155.5) per share and recovering most of the losses since last month, when the affair was first reported.

According to recent reports, the surge helped propel US stock indices to their best day since last year. But in premarket trading on Tuesday, Nvidia fell about 5%, underscoring the volatility of the market and the risks facing the AI sector and the broader tech industry.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The recent volatility around AI, memory chips and other technology stocks has unnerved even the most experienced and bullish investors.

Yet, those seeking a haven away from the United States stock market, which has enjoyed the majority of the AI hype — along with Taiwan and South Korea — are increasingly finding few places to shelter.

Economists warn that this is partly due to the way index funds, including exchange-traded funds (ETFs), work. These funds hold the pensions and other savings of hundreds of millions of passive investors.

These indices have become increasingly exposed to the AI boom.

According to recent reports, most flagship index funds are keen to ride winners, so they automatically buy stocks according to a company's market value. The bigger a company grows, the more of it they hold.

The values of Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet and other US technology giants have benefited from this effect, with many soaring after ChatGPT was first released in late 2022.

According to recent reports, the US also has an outsized position in funds that track the global economy. Nine of the top 10 holdings of the MSCI All Country World Index (ACWI), an index of more than 2,400 firms across 47 developed and emerging markets, are US Major Tech names.

The other is TSMC, a Taiwanese chipmaker that produces 90% of the high-end AI semiconductors.

Together, these 10 holdings make up nearly a quarter of the index.

Although it's a global index, nearly two-thirds of MSCI ACWI's value is in US-listed companies, even though they make up only around a fifth of its firms.

Sources indicate that "A well-diversified portfolio should ... reasonably represent the entire global economy," Gerd Kommer, founder of the Munich-based asset manager Gerd Kommer Invest, told DW.

In a recent development, "That's not the case if 70% of the portfolio is concentrated in just one country — the US. The global economy is more resilient than any national economy.".

Kommer, who is known as Germany's "ETF pope," mentioned investors need exposure to all economic sectors and that no single sector should make up more than a quarter of a portfolio.

Yet, even if investors want to avoid US-dominated World funds altogether, the AI trade still overshadows several other top index funds.

In MSCI's Emerging Market index, for example, the top 10 make up 37.5% of its value and TSMC alone accounts for almost 16%. Tech, chip and internet firms make up eight of the largest holdings, alongside two banks — one Chinese, one Indian.

That matters, according to Dimitri Vayanos, a finance professor at the London School of Economics who studies how passive investing pushes up the prices of the biggest firms.

"My model suggests that the effects of flows into index funds are larger when the large stocks happen to be in the same industry," Vayanos told DW.

When some investors get over-optimistic about a tech giant and push the stock price up, index funds add to that price pressure.

Professional investors then often bet against overpriced stocks, a practice known as "shorting," which helps pull prices back down. But that's far riskier with, say, a tech giant than with a small firm.

"Being short 1% of SpaceX involves much more risk than being short 1% of a small tech giant," stated Vayanos.

Industry observers note that the problem gets worse when the biggest firms are all in the same sector, as they are now. As short-sellers hold back, the biggest stocks climb further, creating what he calls an "amplification-overpricing spiral.".

In a recent development, to cut exposure to AI-related stocks, investors may have to turn to developed market funds outside the US and Southeast Asia. These funds have offered lower returns over the past decade.

In the MSCI Europe, Australasia and Far East (EAFE) index fund, the top 10 holdings make up about 14.5% of the index, about 40% lower than the all-country world index.

EAFE's major holdings include healthcare giant Roche, oil major Shell, HSBC bank and Nestle — the world's largest food and beverage company.

However, its biggest holding, ASML, is still very much part of the AI trade. The Dutch tech firm sells the equipment that firms such as TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron need to make their chips.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, if Monday's rebound in the AI trade is sustained, stock prices may move sharply higher over the next few months. Yet if history is a guide, the bubble will eventually burst, leaving both institutional and passive investors nursing heavy losses.

Kommer warned that if the AI bubble bursts, "in all likelihood it will drag down the global stock market," though the damage would be most severe in tech and AI stocks.

Those hit hardest would be retail investors "with heavy portfolio weights in tech and AI stocks," he mentioned, including "a lot of people who have bought individual AI-related stocks on top of their equity ETFs.".

LSE's Vayanos thinks it is still "certainly safer to hold an ETF than to hold individual stocks.".

But as index providers add mega-IPOs such as SpaceX and Claude-maker Anthropic to benchmarks within weeks of their debut, and money continues to pour into passive funds, he warned that "the conditions are present for the effects of our theory to be even stronger.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that taylor, who would also form The Power Station, enjoyed a solo career and was something of a serial collaborator, stood tall in a golden era for electric guitarists.
  • Forget the Cold War, there was another arms race where the weapons of choice were plugged-in six-strings, with rows of effects pedals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that andy Taylor, the founding guitarist with Duran Duran, who passed away Monday (Nov. 23) following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, aged 65, just might be the most underrated musician to emerge from the early 1980s.

Sources indicate that taylor, who would also form The Power Station, enjoyed a solo career and was something of a serial collaborator, stood tall in a golden era for electric guitarists. Even the slickest commercial pop songs had destructive guitar solos, the type of which seem to be lost to this generation and last.

Forget the Cold War, there was another arms race where the weapons of choice were plugged-in six-strings, with rows of effects pedals. Eddie Van Halen, Steve Vai, Joe Satriani, The Edge, Steve Stevens, Yngwie Malmsteen, Steve Lukather. It was an expansive group, and Andy Taylor was a member in good standing.

Born in Tynemouth and raised in Cullercoats, Northumberland, in north east England, Taylor was the wild boy in Duran Duran – his autobiography from 2008 even carried that title.

Here was a roguish rockstar with fast hands, itchy feet, who didn’t follow trends, but had many, many followers. But because of his breakthrough with Duran Duran, a band that drew a mystifying flood of hate from critics of the time, Taylor’s talents were largely overlooked.

What he did next, couldn’t be ignored.

Duran Duran split into two camps following the release of the 1985 James Bond hit “A View to a Kill.” Andy and John Taylor formed The Power Station, the funk-rock supergroup with Robert Palmer at the front, and Tony Thompson at the back, while Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and Roger Taylor launched Arcadia, a collaborative-stacked project that, in an alternative universe, would’ve been Duran Duran’s fourth studio album.

Industry observers note that with The Power Station, Andy Taylor was unleashed. We got shredding, finger tapping, the works. Taylor contributed to the Duran Duran album from 1986, Notorious, then he was out. Fifteen years later, he returned to the band with original drummer Roger Taylor, to reunite the Fab Five. He contributed to the 2004 album Astronaut, and again on the 2023 collection Danse Macabre.

It has been revealed that the music world learned of his illness when, in 2022, Duran Duran was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Taylor, his bandmates explained, as they read out a letter from the guitarist, was unable to attend due to illness.

Billboard has compiled six deep-dive moments from Andy Taylor’s Hall of Fame career.

Recent findings suggest that in 1984, Duran Duran was on top of the world. The previous year, the band dropped Seven And The Ragged Tiger, their first U.K. No. 1 album. Its opening track, “The Reflex,” gave them a first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The following year, in 1985, another U.S. No. 1 with “A View To A Kill.” A 1984 tour documentary, Sing Blue Silver, a line from the fan favorite Rio album closer “The Chauffeur,” captured the band on the road, but also gave Duranies an unexpected smack to the funnybone. Andy Taylor has one of the standout moments when he ignited an impromptu, running double-entendre joke at a press conference, a response to a question on when he learned to play his instrument. The punchline is a knockout.

Industry observers note that with The Power Station, Andy Taylor was off the leash. The first single, “Some Like It Hot,” showcased his mad skills. With their cover of T-Rex’s “Get It On (Bang a Gong),” he was on fire. Perhaps his finest work is on “Murderess,” which the band performed at the Philadelphia leg of Live Aid in 1985, with Michael Des Barres slotting in on vocal duties when Robert Palmer dropped out. With Des Barres on board, the fourpiece made an appearance on Miami Vice. Check out the studio cut and the live version of “Murderess” below.

During the 1985 recording sessions for The Power Station’s self-titled debut album at the Power Station studio in New York City, Taylor recorded his tasty licks and explosive solos in the control room rather than out in the main live room. The reason behind it was to create an almost-live atmosphere, with producer Bernard Edwards part of his audience. Watch from 3.40 in this behind the scenes footage. “A lead guitarist, their personalities are usually fire,” the late Chic great Edwards explains. “It’s usually pretty hot. And he is a lead guitarist.”.

After splitting with Duran Duran, and moving on from The Power Station (he would contribute to a second album, Living In Fear, released in 1996), Taylor took the natural next step and started a solo career. For the entre, he presented “Take It Easy,” which appeared on the soundtrack for the 1986 feature film American Anthem. It was as different to a Duran Duran song as one could imagine. And Andy, for the first time, was on vocal duties. A full solo album, Thunder, followed in 1987.

Andy Taylor was constantly on the move, recording with Robert Palmer (he played the guitar parts on his 1986 hit “Addicted to Love”), and with the likes of Rod Stewart, the Almighty, Love and Money, Tina Arena, Then Jerico and Belinda Carlisle.

“I was blessed to work with Andy Taylor – such a genius… he played the guitar solo in MAD ABOUT YOU, appears in the video and he made special appearances onstage for some of my first solo demonstrates. What a talent,” writes Carlisle on social media. “Thank you Andy Taylor for the music and all of the joy you brought to the world which will live on forever. I hope you are feeling the love…Godspeed.”.

Taylor appears in the official music video at the 2.07 mark.

In the 1980s, Andy operated Rio’s (also known as Rio Bar), a wine bar and restaurant in Whitley Bay, England. It was, of course, named after the band’s hit sophomore album and its title track. In 1985, a vandal reportedly smashed the venue’s piranha tank, spilling hundreds of gallons of water and letting loose its carnivorous occupants. It’s not known what happened with the fish, but the spot ultimately changed hands.

Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a upcoming study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.

Sources indicate that researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes. They detected at least one of 19 mycotoxins in every product, and many contained multiple toxins.

Industry observers note that mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds. They can enter the food supply when agricultural crops become contaminated during growing, harvesting, or storage.

The investigation was led by scientists at the University of Parma in Italy, with contributions from Cranfield University. The researchers analyzed 212 products, including plant-based meat alternatives (PMBAs) and plant-based beverages (PBBs). The selection covered foods commonly found on supermarket shelves, such as vegan burgers, vegetarian chicken pieces, vegan sausages, and oat, almond, and soy milk.

Although the findings highlight how widespread these naturally occurring contaminants can be, the researchers also identified an vital reassuring detail. Every product contained mycotoxin concentrations below recommended European Union guideline levels, which the team remarked reflected the high food quality standards maintained by the UK food industry.

Why Plant-Based Foods Can Contain Fungal Toxins.

It has been revealed that many of the ingredients used to manufacture plant-based foods are particularly susceptible to fungal contamination. Grains, legumes, and seeds can encounter mold in fields or storage facilities, creating opportunities for mycotoxins to develop before the ingredients reach food manufacturers.

Sources indicate that unlike bacteria or viruses, mycotoxins are chemical substances produced by certain fungi. Their presence in food does not necessarily mean the product contains living mold, and detecting a toxin does not automatically mean the food is unsafe. The potential health risk depends on factors such as the type of toxin, its concentration, and how much a person consumes over time.

This distinction is especially crucial for people who eat plant-based products frequently. Someone whose diet regularly includes meat substitutes, dairy alternatives, grains, and legumes may encounter these substances through several different foods rather than a single source.

Could Repeated Exposure Pose Health Risks?

While the concentrations detected in the UK products were below recommended EU guidelines, researchers say the potential effects of repeated exposure deserve closer attention.

Recent findings suggest that earlier studies have suggested that consuming small amounts of mycotoxins regularly may contribute to cumulative exposure and potentially increase health risks. In other words, assessing a single product may not provide a complete picture of a person's overall dietary exposure.

Recent findings suggest that eating one of these products occasionally is unlikely to cause problems based on the levels reported. However, a diet that relies heavily or exclusively on plant-based foods could involve repeated exposure to mycotoxins from numerous ingredients and products. Researchers say understanding the combined effects is key for evaluating possible long-term health consequences.

The severity of mycotoxin exposure varies depending on the compounds involved and the amount consumed. At sufficiently high or harmful exposure levels, certain mycotoxins can damage the liver and kidneys, interfere with normal immune system function, and increase the risk of cancer.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced findings do not establish that the tested products cause these conditions. Instead, they provide information that scientists can use to estimate how much exposure consumers may receive through their diets and develop more accurate food safety risk assessments for the UK population.

Scientists Call for Better Monitoring of Plant-Based Ingredients.

Sources indicate that andrea Patriarca, Senior Lecturer in Mycology at Cranfield University, emphasized that mycotoxins are a natural part of the food environment and should not discourage people from eating a varied diet. Mycology is the branch of biology devoted to studying fungi, including molds and yeasts.

"Mycotoxins occur naturally in foods and cannot be completely avoided. As consumers, we should not be frightened or deterred from enjoying a variety of products.

In a recent development, however, a significant concern arises when newly introduced foods enter the market, as there are at the moment no established regulations to monitor mycotoxins. We collaborate closely with various sectors in the food industry, from farmers to food companies, to help implement effective mycotoxin management integrated within food safety standards. The data from our research helps food safety organizations in assessing risks, particularly in complex multi-ingredient products.

We are right now collaborating with the University of Parma to evaluate the risks faced by the population based on different dietary habits. Our aim is to advise policymakers and raise awareness among vulnerable consumers.".

The researchers are particularly interested in how food safety monitoring can keep pace with the growing range of plant-based products. Foods made from multiple ingredients present additional challenges because each component may introduce different contaminants, making overall exposure more difficult to assess.

Their work also underscores the importance of monitoring raw materials throughout the food production process. Identifying and controlling contamination before ingredients are combined into finished products could help manufacturers manage potential risks more effectively.

What the Findings Mean for Plant-Based Diets.

The discovery of fungal toxins in all 212 products highlights the importance of studying dietary exposure across multiple foods, rather than evaluating each product in isolation.

For consumers, the results are not a reason to abandon vegan or vegetarian foods. The concentrations measured were below recommended EU guidelines, and the researchers stress that mycotoxins cannot be completely eliminated from the food supply.

Instead, the study points to the need for continued research into how different eating habits influence exposure, particularly among people who depend heavily on plant-based products. The University of Parma and Cranfield University are continuing their collaboration to investigate these dietary patterns, identify potentially vulnerable groups, and provide evidence that can inform future food safety policies.

The research, titled "Mycotoxin contamination in plant-based beverages and meat alternatives: A survey of the UK market," was published in the journal Food Control.

The study was conducted as part of the European Union-funded Horizon Europe FunShield4Med project (HORIZON-WIDERA-2021-ACCESS-03), Grant Agreement No 101079173.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25).

The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe rolled out atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024. Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos, a "rubble pile" asteroid, and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test, which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid.

Sources indicate that hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25). Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency.

It has been revealed that at Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth.

The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids.

Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects.

"ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement. "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact?

"Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test.".

ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse.

Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos.

Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments.

Through Hera, scientists hope to refine planetary defense techniques so that, should the time ever come, humanity has options for defending itself against incoming space rocks like the one that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

"Through many years of hard work our international collaboration managed to do just that, and for the very highest of intentions: to help make Earth safer," stated Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Americans have grown used to corporate executives treading the well-worn paths of the Northeast corridor to convene alongside elected officials in Washington, DC, and discuss geopolitics, policy and all that’s in-between.
  • In 2017, major CEOs from across the country came together to oppose North Carolina’s transgender bathroom law.
  • After the deadly attack on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, many of corporate America’s biggest names denounced the rioters and pledged to halt their political giving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Americans have grown used to corporate executives treading the well-worn paths of the Northeast corridor to convene alongside elected officials in Washington, DC, and discuss geopolitics, policy and all that’s in-between.

In 2017, major CEOs from across the country came together to oppose North Carolina’s transgender bathroom law. In 2019, they called abortion bans “bad for business.”.

After the deadly attack on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, many of corporate America’s biggest names denounced the rioters and pledged to halt their political giving.

Recently, more than 1,000 companies promised to voluntarily curtail their operations in Russia in protest of Moscow’s war on Ukraine.

Dick’s Sporting Goods stopped selling semi-automatic, assault-style rifles at stores and Citigroup put latest restrictions on gun sales by business customers after the mass shooting at a high school in Parkland, Florida, in 2018.

A year later, after mass shootings at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas, and a nightclub in Dayton, Ohio, Walmart ended handgun ammunition sales.

Corporate leadership has long been vocal on the matter of gun control – in 2019 and again this past summer nearly 150 major companies – including Lululemon, Lyft, Bain Capital, Bloomberg LP, Permanente Medical Group and Unilever – called gun violence a “public health crisis” and demanded that the US Senate pass legislation to address it.

That’s why corporate America’s silence in the wake of the latest mass shooting at a school in Nashville is so jarring. The United States has come to rely on the increasing power of large corporations as political advocates.

Industry observers note that but Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, a vocal advocate of corporate social responsibility who has a direct line to major CEOs around the globe, said that top executives are forlorn. Their previous efforts haven’t done much to push the needle on gun control legislation and without more backing, they don’t know what else they can do at the moment, he said.

Before the Bell spoke with Sonnenfeld, who runs Yale School of Management’s Chief Executive Leadership Institute, a nonprofit educational and research institute focused on CEO leadership and corporate governance.

This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

Before the Bell: CEOs have been quiet about gun reform since the latest mass school shooting in Nashville, have you heard anything about plans to speak out?

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld: Where is everybody else? Where is all of civil society? CEOs are just one group of people and it’s like we’re turning to them to be our saviors on every topic. They’ve joined causes with valor and nobility but they can’t just be taking cause after cause as if there’s nobody else in society. The social change that happened in the 1960s wasn’t being led primarily by CEOs. Social changes really happened when we saw the interfaith activity of clergy locking arms and canvassing legislators. We saw campuses alive and aroused. Where’s all the student activism?

Sources indicate that the CEOs are still the most active even if they’re less active than they were six months ago. They’re not there as hired hands of shareholders to fill the role of politicians and civic leaders. They’re there to join that chorus, but they don’t want to be the only one singing.

So is this what you’re hearing from top CEOs? Have they gotten tired of advocating?

Recent findings suggest that I just got off of a CEO call on voting rights and this morning we had a forum on sustainability – CEOs are still the most active on these fronts. It’s the same thing on immigration reform. If a CEO was working an 18 hour day on a 12 day week, they still couldn’t address all of the issues that need addressing.

The nation’s CEOs are waiting for everybody else to join them. They don’t need to restate something they’ve already stated. They’ve jumped in the pool, where’s everybody else?

So what do you think has led to this complacency amongst Americans and the growing reliance on CEOs to advocate on our behalf?

According to recent reports, they’ve taken a very strong stance and they’ve gone out further than the general public. They are where the general public is on surveys, but they’re not where the general public is on action in the streets. So we’re ready for others to now do something. Enough already on saying ‘what are the CEOs doing?’ Social capital is as valuable as financial capital. CEOs understand that in their soul, they want there to be social capital. They want there to be public trust, but they need the rest of civil society to join them. And that’s their frustration.

It sounds like CEOs are frustrated?

But don’t these CEOs hold the purse strings in terms of donating to powerful politicians?

In a recent development, you would think that, but since the 2020 elections much less of campaign contributions have come from substantial business. Since the 2021 run on the Capitol, a lot of businesses either had an official moratorium or they’ve given mere pennies to politicians. The common impression on the street that CEOs are controlling campaign purses strings is 100% wrong.

Tesla reported. a modest 4% rise in sales in the first quarter compared to the final three months of last year, despite a series of price cuts on its lower priced vehicles and talk by CEO Elon Musk about strong demand at those lower prices.

The first quarter also marked the fourth straight quarter that Tesla has produced more vehicles than it has delivered to customers. Some of that may be due to the ramp up in production at two fresh factories, one in Texas, the other in Germany, which opened last spring, and a lag between that increased production and sales.

Tesla remarked there was an increase in the number of its more expensive models, the Model S and Model X, in transit to Europe, the Middle East and Africa, as well as to the Asia Pacific region.

But it does mean that over the last 12 months Tesla has produced 78,000 more cars than it has sold, suggesting that talk of strong demand by Tesla executives may not be backed up by the numbers.

It has been revealed that “Early this year, we had a price adjustment. After that, we actually generated a huge demand, more than we can produce, really,” remarked Tom Zhu, Tesla’s executive in charge of global production and sales. “And as Elon said, as long as you offer a product with value at affordable price, you don’t have to worry about demand.”.

It has been revealed that power plants, train stations, shopping centers, warehouses and residential buildings: The massive Russian attacks on civilian targets across Ukraine continue unabated. Industrial facilities have also come under fire, affecting German companies.

Industry observers note that at the 9th German-Ukrainian Business Forum, held in Berlin on November 20, Gierlichs described the situation on the ground. Together with two other German business associations, the AHK had invited around 500 participants from politics and industry, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi.

According to the AHK, just over 2,000 German companies are active in Ukraine. German direct investment in the country totals around €1 billion ($1.1 billion). The situation remains critical due to the ongoing attacks, Gierlichs noted. "We are preparing for a difficult winter.".

After posting comparatively strong growth rates in recent years, Ukraine's economy has slowed sharply since the summer.

"The intensified Russian attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure and production capacity in recent months have significantly worsened the economic outlook," according to the latest analysis by the Kyiv School of Economics (KSE), which warns of "substantial risks.".

It has been revealed that energy supplies are under strain, and electricity remains in short supply. Companies are also grappling with a worker shortage, as many people have been mobilized for military service or have fled abroad to escape the attacks. German business leaders also cite burdensome approval processes and unclear regulations in Ukraine.

"Not a single German company has left Ukraine since the start of this war," Merz emphasized at the business forum. He also pointed out that "in 2025, trade between Germany and Ukraine exceeded €12 billion, an increase of 4.4% compared with the previous year.".

Military cooperation currently tops the agenda in German-Ukrainian relations. Germany continues to supply large quantities of defense equipment, but fresh capabilities are increasingly being developed through joint ventures. At the business forum, held at the House of German Business Associations in Berlin, the long-range combat drone "Anubis," produced by the German-Ukrainian joint venture Auterion Airlogix, was displayed in the foyer. The drone was developed in Ukraine and the software in Germany.

Recent findings suggest that A total of 5,000 drones are to be produced near Munich. This marks the first time Germany has established industrial-scale production of heavy attack drones on its own soil. "Through this cooperation, Germany's technological capacity for innovation is expanding in ways that would have been unimaginable just a few years ago," Merz stated.

The chancellor is convinced that cooperation between the two countries will also benefit Germany's civilian industries. "What we invest in Ukraine today will be repaid many times over through stability, export opportunities, joint projects, and economic growth," he remarked.

According to recent reports, for foreign companies operating in Ukraine, it is a continuous balancing act. On the one hand, substantial risks persist; on the other, Ukraine represents a land of opportunity, with a market size virtually unmatched anywhere else in Europe. In February 2025, the European Commission and the Ukrainian government estimated that Ukraine would need $524 billion in funding for reconstruction and recovery over the following 10 years. This figure has likely grown even larger since then.

In this context, Ukraine is increasingly seen not merely as a recipient of aid but also as a potential future business destination. The country aims to modernize its economy, bring it into alignment with EU standards, and achieve deeper integration into the European single market over the long term.

"We see significant opportunities in the defense industry, the energy sector, infrastructure, information technology and many other industries," Ukrainian Prime Minister Koretskyi stated in Berlin.

It has been revealed that "German expertise and Ukrainian drive, combined with unity and determination, make for a powerful partnership," Oliver Gierlichs noted. However, achieving this will require greater support, the AHK president emphasized. "Companies need reliable financing and investment guarantees, as well as effective instruments to protect themselves against war-related risks.".

Reliable logistics, predictable business conditions, and faster administrative procedures will also be essential, he added.

At the business forum, Chancellor Merz pledged support in these areas while also calling on Ukraine to pursue further reforms, particularly to strengthen the rule of law and combat corruption. "These reforms are a prerequisite for additional financial assistance and investment.".

Another challenge stems from the differing interests of the partners. German companies are seeking to expand into newly introduced markets, while their Ukrainian counterparts seek technology transfers and local production to keep as much value creation as possible in the country. "Export fees or legal restrictions on the transfer of intellectual property rights stand in the way of joint innovation efforts," the chancellor cautioned.

Representatives of Ukrainian business associations estimate that the private sector could cover up to 40% of Ukraine's reconstruction costs in the long term. For now, however, many projects rely on support from international development banks, government guarantees, or public funding programs. Without such support, many investments would be difficult to undertake.

In principle, business investment follows a straightforward model: Companies commit their own capital and bear the losses if a venture fails commercially. When bank loans are involved, the risk is initially shared by the company and the lending institution. Government-backed projects are different. When investment guarantees are in place, companies are compensated for any losses incurred.

Recent findings suggest that this does not apply when companies incur losses as a result of their own business decisions. Compensation may, however, be available in cases involving political actions, such as expropriation, or when war destroys assets and disrupts operations. Under a government guarantee, the taxpayer ultimately bears the risk in such circumstances. By the end of 2025, the German government had provided investment guarantees covering a total investment volume of €558 million ($611 million) in Ukraine.

German companies hoping to benefit from Ukraine's reconstruction need to establish partnerships and build a long-term presence in the country now. After all, the competition is already heating up. At the German-Ukrainian Business Forum, participants noted that German business leaders have often been more risk-averse than their counterparts from Turkey, India and China. International interest in Ukraine's reconstruction is considerable, and German companies are far from the only ones vying for contracts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A latest approach to weight loss could help the body burn more fat while preserving muscle, potentially overcoming one of the major drawbacks of existing obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, have identified a compound that increases the amount of energy the body uses rather than simply reducing how much food a person eats.

Recent findings suggest that in experiments with mice, the compound improved blood sugar regulation, reduced harmful blood fats, and helped obese animals lose fat without a significant reduction in lean muscle mass. It also increased energy expenditure by up to 18%, even though the mice did not become more physically active or experience an increase in body temperature.

Industry observers note that the findings, published in Science Advances, suggest a promising new direction for treating obesity, diabetes, and fatty liver disease. The experimental compound also appeared to enhance the benefits of popular weight-loss medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy when the treatments were used together. However, its effectiveness and safety have not yet been established in humans.

A Different Approach to Weight Loss Than Ozempic.

Over the past five years, medications known as GLP-1 drugs have transformed the treatment of obesity and other metabolic conditions, including diabetes and fatty liver disease. Drugs marketed as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound have helped many patients achieve substantial weight loss while improving their ability to regulate blood sugar.

It has been revealed that despite these benefits, the medications have important limitations. Nausea and other digestive problems can make treatment difficult for some patients. Because these drugs reduce appetite and food consumption, they can also increase the risk of inadequate nutrition and loss of muscle mass. Over time, losing too much muscle can contribute to weakness, frailty, and other health complications.

Berkeley researchers wanted to investigate a fundamentally different strategy. Rather than focusing on reducing calorie intake, they explored whether it would be possible to increase the amount of energy the body burns.

This process, known as energy expenditure, includes the calories used to maintain basic bodily functions, regulate metabolism, and support everyday activities. Increasing energy expenditure could potentially help people lose weight without relying exclusively on eating less.

Recent findings suggest that "Body weight responds to two levers: taking in fewer calories, or spending more energy," said Anders Näär, a professor of metabolic biology and nutrition at UC Berkeley and senior author of the study. "GLP-1s work almost entirely on the first, so we went after the second.".

A Compound That Burns Fat While Preserving Muscle.

The researchers focused on a molecule called 5-tetradecyloxy-2-furoic acid (TOFA), which has an unusual combination of effects on the body's metabolism.

TOFA interferes with the production of lipids, a broad category of fatty substances that includes cholesterol and triglycerides. These molecules serve vital functions, but excessive levels of certain lipids can contribute to metabolic disorders and cardiovascular disease.

In a recent development, at the same time, TOFA activates genes involved in taking up and burning fat for energy. This combination allows the compound to influence both how the body produces fat and how it uses fat as fuel.

In a recent development, in mice, treatment with TOFA produced several encouraging results. The animals became more sensitive to insulin, the hormone that helps move glucose from the bloodstream into cells. Improved insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to control blood sugar, an important benefit for people with diabetes or insulin resistance.

The compound also lowered triglyceride levels and improved characteristics of fatty liver disease, a condition in which excess fat accumulates inside liver cells and can eventually interfere with liver function.

Sources indicate that perhaps most notably, obese mice treated with TOFA lost weight primarily through reductions in body fat, without experiencing significant losses of lean muscle mass. This distinction could be especially valuable because maintaining muscle is important for strength, mobility, and long-term metabolic health.

How TOFA Increases Energy Burning by 18%.

Although TOFA was originally discovered in the 1970s, the new research uncovered additional properties that could make it particularly useful for treating metabolic disease.

The compound belongs to a group of substances known as ACC inhibitors. These compounds interfere with enzymes that help the body manufacture fatty acids, effectively slowing the production of certain fats.

Other ACC inhibitors have previously advanced to mid-stage clinical trials, but none has been approved to treat metabolic diseases. One major obstacle has been an unexpected side effect: many of these compounds increase triglycerides in the blood, potentially raising the risk of heart problems.

In a recent development, the Berkeley team discovered that TOFA does more than inhibit ACC. It also activates two cellular receptors called PPARα and PPARδ, which help regulate the genes responsible for fat metabolism.

Recent findings suggest that these receptors function as molecular switches. When activated, they stimulate processes that allow cells to absorb fatty acids and break them down to produce energy. In effect, TOFA simultaneously reduces the production of certain fats and encourages the body to burn fat that is already available.

According to recent reports, in mice, this activity increased energy expenditure by as much as 18%, without requiring additional physical activity or raising body temperature. Unlike other ACC inhibitors, TOFA also did not cause triglyceride levels to rise, potentially because of its additional effects on fat metabolism.

It has been revealed that "TOFA appears to engage a coordinated metabolic response," mentioned study first author Justin Y. Lee, a postdoctoral student at UCSF who conducted the research as a Ph.D. student at Berkeley. "It is not simply blocking lipid synthesis. It is also activating energy expenditure pathways that may help the body handle excess lipid and glucose more effectively.".

Sources indicate that to understand whether these effects could be reproduced with separate treatments, the scientists gave mice a combination of two different compounds. One blocked lipid production, while the other stimulated energy expenditure.

According to recent reports, surprisingly, this two-compound approach was less effective at improving overall metabolic health than TOFA alone. The finding suggests that TOFA's ability to influence multiple metabolic processes through a single molecule may be an key part of its effectiveness.

Could TOFA Make Ozempic and Wegovy More Effective?

The researchers also investigated whether TOFA could improve the results of existing GLP-1 medications.

They tested the compound alongside semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, as well as tirzepatide, which is marketed as Mounjaro and Zepbound.

Industry observers note that these medications primarily help people lose weight by reducing appetite and food intake. TOFA, by contrast, targets the other side of the energy balance equation by increasing how much energy the body expends.

In a recent development, when the researchers combined TOFA with these medications in mice, the results were more favorable than those produced by either treatment alone. The combinations led to greater improvements in body weight, blood glucose regulation, insulin levels, and triglycerides.

This suggests that treatments targeting calorie intake and energy expenditure could potentially work together to produce stronger metabolic benefits.

"In our combination experiments, TOFA worked additively or synergistically with the GLP-1 appetite-suppressing drugs, so we view it as complementary rather than as a replacement," Näär remarked.

In a recent development, in other words, the researchers do not necessarily envision TOFA replacing medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy. Instead, it could eventually become an additional treatment that helps address obesity and related metabolic conditions through a different biological mechanism.

A Promising Discovery, but Human Trials Are Still Needed.

Sources indicate that despite the encouraging results, the researchers emphasize that TOFA remains an experimental compound. All the findings so far come from animal studies, and scientists have not yet established whether it is safe or effective in humans.

Further research will be necessary to determine whether the same metabolic improvements can be achieved in people and whether the treatment could offer meaningful advantages over existing medications.

To help move the research toward potential clinical applications, the Berkeley scientists have established a biotechnology company called ReRx Therapeutics. The effort has received support from the university's life sciences entrepreneurship network, including Nucleate and Berkeley SkyDeck.

Industry observers note that if the findings eventually translate to humans, TOFA could represent an notable addition to the growing range of treatments for obesity and diabetes. By encouraging the body to use more energy while helping preserve muscle, the compound points toward a potentially different way to achieve healthier weight loss.

The research was funded through discretionary resources provided by UC Berkeley, with additional support from the UCSF Liver Center and the University of Michigan Animal Phenotyping Core.

Sources indicate that additional authors include Chi Zhu, Melissa A. Boldridge, Rachelle L. Stark, Lei Xu, Federico Gonzalez, Xin Tang, Kaitlyn T. Dang and Kook Son of Berkeley; Gracia Bonilla, Kashish Chetal and Ruslan I. Sadreyev of Massachusetts General Hospital; Kosuke Watari and Michael Karin of the University of California, San Diego; Christina Papa and Bilal N. Sheikh of the Helmholtz Center Munich; Prabha Ibrahim of ReRx Therapeutics.

Sources indicate that tributes are flooding in for Andy Taylor, the brawny founding guitarist for Duran Duran and The Power Station, who has passed away after a years-long battle with prostate cancer. He was 65. Explore Andy Taylor Duran Duran See latest videos, charts and news.

See latest videos, charts and news.

Recent findings suggest that “I was blessed to work with Andy Taylor – such a genius… he played the guitar solo in MAD ABOUT YOU, appears in the video and he made special appearances onstage for some of my first solo reveals. “Thank you Andy Taylor for the music and all of the joy you brought to the world which will live on forever. I hope you are feeling the love…Godspeed.”.

Legendary Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant joined Taylor on stage in Oxfordshire, England back in 2023, at a charity fundraiser gig for The Cancer Awareness Trust. “A tough fighter, Andy Taylor,” he recounts, “like so many…some of us get through…condolences to his tribe,” he writes.

Fellow axeman Steve Stevens, the longtime talisman of Billy Idol, was heartbroken on the news. “F#ck cancer,” he writes. “Have so many memories with Andy. In a recent development, duran Duran and Spandau Ballet were, for a time, the British second invasion’s pin-up boys. “Spandau Ballet are deeply saddened by the passing of Andy Taylor,” reads a message from the pop group. “Andy was a hugely talented musician and an vital part of the British music scene that we were all proud to be part of. Our thoughts are with his family, friends and fans around the world.”.

Spandau Ballet’s co-founder and songwriter Gary Kemp had his own words. “So sad to hear the news of Andy’s passing,” he writes. “A great player who set the tone for the eighties and influenced many of us along the way with his sparse staccato style. Like Duran Duran, UB40 for formed in Birmingham, England. “We have just heard the sad news that Andy Taylor, Duran Duran guitarist, has lost his long battle with Cancer,” a post reads. “Our thoughts are with his band mates and his family. Another one gone too soon! Big Love UB40.”.

Sources indicate that veteran British singer Michael Des Barres stepped up when Robert Palmer stepped out of The Power Station, the funk-rock band Andy and John Taylor formed in 1985 when Duran Duran was on hiatus. “He was a tough and rocking guitar player,” writes Des Barres. “He knew what he wanted, and he gave it to us. I was able to learn 22 songs in five days of rehearsal with the Power Station because of Andy‘s tremendous enthusiasm and professionalism. Simply put, he loved rock ‘n’ roll. RIP- My friend.”.

Terri Nunn’s Berlin paid tribute with a lyric to the band’s 1993 comeback classic “Ordinary World,” which featured Warren Cuccurullo on guitar. “Where is the life that I recognise? (Gone away) RIP #AndyTaylor.”.

The Dandy Warhols shared a picture of Courtney Taylor-Taylor in his happy place, with a glass of red in his hand, and Andy Taylor at his side.

In a recent development, andy Taylor (no relation with John and Roger) had multiple stints in Duran Duran, scoring 13 hits on the Billboard Hot 100, including two No. 1s: “The Reflex” in 1984 and “A View to a Kill” in 1985. The group’s beloved second album Rio album (which housed “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “Save a Prayer,” and the title track) hit the Billboard 200 in 1982 and remained on the chart for a whopping 128 weeks.

Industry observers note that as a member of The Power Station, he earned three top 40 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985, and as a soloist, he scored two entries on the chart: “Take It Easy” (No. 24 in 1986) and “When the Rain Comes Down” (No. 73 in 1986).

Taylor was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022 in absentia due to his illness, which his bandmates unveiled from the platform of their induction speech for the very first time.

Sources indicate that it was the rocker’s former bandmates who shared the tragic news “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story,” the group wrote on their website and on Instagram. “From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.”.

The message continued, “His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”.

Also, Taylor’s wife, Tracey, shared a statement: “To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather,” she wrote. “He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first.”.

Andy is also survived by his children — Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew — and grandson Albie.

#196634. A Journey Through the Absurd Hell of Trump’s Third-Country Deportations
